full_question: A 25-year-old female patient with a history of skin rash after sun exposure and occasional polyarthritis in the joints of the hands, controlled with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, presents with general malaise, progressive feeling of generalized weakness and pallor for the last 15 days. Laboratory tests showed hemoglobin 7 g/dL, MCV 108 mm/h, 150,000 platelets/mm3, 3000 leukocytes/mm3, elevated LDH, undetectable haptoglobin. In the case of choosing a single diagnostic test indicate which of the following determinations should be performed first:

options.5: Folic acid.

generated_explanation: The patient presents with macrocytic anemia (MCV 108 mm/h) and pancytopenia (anemia, leukopenia, mild thrombocytopenia), along with elevated LDH and undetectable haptoglobin, suggesting significant red blood cell destruction. While undetectable haptoglobin strongly points to peripheral hemolysis often seen in autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA), the combination of severe macrocytic anemia and pancytopenia is highly characteristic of megaloblastic anemia, caused by vitamin B12 or folic acid deficiency. Severe megaloblastic anemia can also cause elevated LDH (due to ineffective erythropoiesis) and, in some cases, significant peripheral hemolysis of defective red cells leading to undetectable haptoglobin. Folic acid deficiency is a common and treatable cause of this comprehensive hematologic picture, offering a unified explanation for all findings.
